claims.text: The measured excess on this trip's own trace is 0.84 km: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 4.04 km against the booked optimal of 3.2 km recorded on the trip record, which is 26.25% of optimal. Both limbs of the POL-RD-01 establishment test therefore pass — 0.84 km is greater than the 0.8 km absolute threshold, and 26.25% is greater than the 20% proportional threshold. The route deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's evidence.

The governing distance field is the trace figure, not the trip record's rounded convenience copy. trip_record.actual_distance_km is 4.0 km, which yields exactly 0.80 km of excess — not greater than 0.8 km — and would fail the absolute limb outright. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km governing precisely because these two fields straddle the threshold, and it expressly forbids citing actual_distance_km for the threshold test. The 4.04 km trace figure is the only admissible measure here.

Because the deviation is established and nothing excuses it, the refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 on a METERED fare. recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 3.2 km optimal + 0.28 x 6.0 min optimal) x the 1.0 surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, plus the 0.80 platform fee = 8.68 SGD. charged_total is 9.70 SGD, so the refund is 9.70 - 8.68 = 1.02 SGD, rounded up to the payable 1.05 SGD. The fare ledger's own derived money block records 1.0200 before rounding and 1.05 payable, and there is no ERP or fixed surcharge to add.

That refund is above the 0.50 SGD de-minimis floor (the ledger's own below_de_minimis flag is false) and is 10.5% of charged_total, far below the 90% share that would make it a FULL_REFUND. The only outcome the arithmetic licenses is PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.05 SGD to the rider. The present state leaves the rider carrying the whole 9.70 SGD — payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00 — and NO_ACTION would leave her there, so a monetary partial is required.

Nothing on this record exculpates the excess. There is no traffic advisory at all: EV-ADVIS-02820-01 is MISSING under the admissibility pre-pass with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so no road, segment or validity window can be tested and POL-RD-03 is unavailable — the driver's 'one-way streets' theory has no advisory record to rest on. The chat log EV-CHAT-02820 carries zero messages over the whole trip, so there is no rider instruction of the kind POL-RD-04(a) to (c) requires, no timestamped request and no waypoint_hint to corroborate. I disclose that EV-ADVIS-02820-01 is impaired at weight 0.0; I cite it only for its absence, which POL-GEN-02 makes citable.

The driver's answer — 'one-way streets' — is an uncited traffic assertion and it discharges nothing. It names no advisory and no evidence ID, so under POL-RD-13(1) it is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5): an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, and the absence of an artifact no party has cited is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction in it. Under POL-RD-08 the burden shifted to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause, and he has pointed to neither. The assertion carries no weight, the deviation stands at the measured figure, and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07. It carries 46 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval against a 10-second expected interval, over 100.0% coverage, with an empty gaps array and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds — so limbs (a), (b) and (c) are all clear. No independent corroboration is therefore required, POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged, and the excess may be established on the trace alone under POL-RD-08(b) on this unimpaired artifact at weight 1.0.

The rider carries her burden under POL-RD-08 and discharges both limbs. The three artifacts describe the same trip: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown each carry trip identifier TRP-02820, with the 10:52:03 pickup start matching the first trace fix. The excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. Her profile does not raise the additional-corroboration condition either: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the 4 that clause names, so nothing beyond the trace is required. The driver's side of the burden remains undischarged.

No other route-deviation clause moves the number in the driver's favour. The fare model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11's upfront-pricing bar on distance refunds does not apply and the rider's loss on the distance and time lines is real money. The trip record shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null with amended_optimal_distance_km null, so POL-RD-05 has no amended endpoints and no re-quote to run, and vehicle_type is RYDE_X rather than RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not displace the 3.2 km optimal. The baseline for POL-RD-01 stays at 3.2 km.

The fare breakdown charges no ERP or tolls — erp_gantries is empty, the erp_lines total is 0.00 SGD and the off-optimal-route total is 0.00 SGD — so there is no off-route pass-through to refund separately and nothing to double-count against the POL-RD-02 figure. The 1.02 SGD refund is distance and time only, exactly as POL-RD-09(1) requires.

I concede that the deviation on this trip is not MATERIAL: at 0.84 km it is far short of the 8.0 km material threshold and at 26.25% it is far short of the 50% material threshold, so POL-RD-06 is not triggered by the POL-RD-01 finding and no FULL_REFUND uplift is available to the rider. I do not ask for one. The rider's remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial of 1.05 SGD, and I ask only for the amount the arithmetic yields.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires on this record, so the rider's refund should issue rather than be held. Trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is unimpaired so limb (3) is clear; the timestamps are ordered and consistent across artifacts (10:45:30 requested, 10:52:03 started, 10:59:33 ended) so limb (4) is clear; the refund of 1.02 SGD is far below the 150.00 SGD ceiling and below charged_total; and no charge line lacks a counterpart, because the ERP line set is empty and the ledger has 0 ERP lines. The disputed amount does not need a human reviewer to be held — it needs to be refunded.

claims.text: The excess on this trip is 0.84 km against a 3.2 km optimal route, or 26.25% — it clears POL-RD-01's 0.8 km absolute floor by roughly 40 metres and sits far below the 50%-or-8.0 km materiality threshold. The deviation is therefore established but not MATERIAL, so POL-RD-06's uplift and conduct-referral limbs are never engaged and the matter is confined to the POL-RD-02 arithmetic on the trace figure the clause makes governing.

POL-RD-06's pattern test fails on the driver's own numbers: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 408 — a ratio of 0.00 where the clause asks for 0.05, and no approach to its 3-flag alternative. No repeat-deviation pattern is established, so the rider gains no FULL_REFUND uplift, the thin margins in this case are not resolved against the driver, and no conduct referral issues; POL-GEN-01 confines this artifact to that single test and bars any wider adverse use of the profile.

The recovery is bounded by the arithmetic, not by the rider's framing. The ledger records total_charged of SGD 9.70 and the POL-RD-02 recomputation on the 3.2 km optimal route — (3.80 + 0.75 x 3.2 + 0.28 x 6.0) at the 1.0 surge multiplier recorded on the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee — comes to SGD 8.68, a difference of SGD 1.02. That is a fraction of the SGD 2.00 actually contested and nothing like the $9.70 quoted in the claim; a 0.84 km excess cannot be converted into the whole fare, and POL-GEN-03 entitles the rider to no more than a partial refund of the contested amount.

Nothing may be added on top of that figure. The trip was METERED, carried a 1.0 surge multiplier, zero ERP or toll charges, no airport surcharge and no gantry lines, and the fare ledger reconciles to total_charged. POL-RD-09 has no off-route or phantom gantry to correct, and under POL-RD-09(1) any off-route ERP is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund and must never be added to it.

The gps_trace is complete and unimpaired — 46 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval, 100.0% coverage, a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds and no straight-line jump between consecutive fixes — so it is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), no escalation under POL-RD-10(3) arises, and the excess stands on an artifact admitted at full weight with nothing left to corroborate.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver, this is the ruling on trip TRP-02820.

THE DEVIATION IS ESTABLISHED. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02820, full weight) measures 4.04 km against the booked optimal route of 3.2 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-02820): an excess of 0.84 km, which is 26.25% of optimal. That clears both limbs of POL-RD-01 — more than 0.8 km absolute and more than 20% proportional — so the deviation stands. The trace figure governs and the trip record's rounded 4.0 km copy may not be used for the threshold test; it would have yielded exactly 0.80 km and failed the absolute limb. The excess is far below the materiality thresholds (50% of optimal, or 8.0 km), so this is not a MATERIAL deviation and POL-RD-06's uplift and conduct-review limbs are not engaged.

NOTHING EXCUSES THE EXCESS. The chat log EV-CHAT-02820 holds zero messages, so there is no rider-requested detour within POL-RD-04(a) to (c). The driver's 'one-way streets' statement names no advisory and no evidence ID; the only advisory slot, EV-ADVIS-02820-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. No amendment under POL-RD-05, no upfront-quote bar under POL-RD-11 (the fare is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null), and no pooled baseline under POL-RD-12 (vehicle_type is RYDE_X). No ERP or toll line was charged, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to correct.

THE REFUND IS ARITHMETIC. Under POL-RD-02 on a METERED fare: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 3.2 km optimal + 0.28 x 6.0 min optimal) x the 1.0 surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, plus the 0.80 platform fee = SGD 8.68. charged_total = SGD 9.70. Refund = 9.70 - 8.68 = SGD 1.02, rounded up to SGD 1.05. That is above the SGD 0.50 de-minimis floor and 10.5% of charged_total, well below the 90% that would make a full refund, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 1.05. The present state has the rider carrying the whole SGD 9.70 (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), so NO_ACTION would leave her there.

NO DRIVER COMPENSATION. The billed distance (4.0 km) falls short of the trace (4.04 km) by only 0.04 km, far under the 1.0 km threshold in POL-RD-04, so no compensation is payable.

NO ESCALATION AND NO REFERRAL. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 (46 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s); the timestamps are ordered; the refund is far under the SGD 150.00 ceiling and under charged_total; and no charge line lacks a counterpart. POL-RD-13 confirms the driver's uncited traffic excuse is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation, because he cited no advisory identifier. No POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral issues (no repeat pattern: deviation_flags_90d 0 against 408 completed trips), and no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral issues (no phantom line).

Rider and driver: trip TRP-02820 carries a route deviation and a small refund is due to the rider.

DISTANCE (POL-RD-01). The governing figure is the trace, not the trip record's rounded copy. EV-GPS-02820 records trace_distance_km 4.04 km; trip_record.actual_distance_km 4.0 km may not be cited for the threshold test. Against the booked optimal of 3.2 km (EV-TRIP-02820) the excess is 0.84 km, or 26.25%. Both limbs pass (0.84 > 0.8 km absolute; 26.25% > 20% proportional), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is not MATERIAL (well under 8.0 km and 50%), so POL-RD-06's FULL_REFUND uplift and its conduct referral are never engaged; on the driver's own profile the pattern test also fails (deviation_flags_90d 0 against 408 completed trips).

REFUND (POL-RD-02). The fare is METERED (EV-FARE-02820), not upfront, so the arithmetic runs. recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 3.2 km + 0.28 x 6.0 min) x 1.0 surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier + 0.80 platform fee = 8.68 SGD. charged_total is 9.70 SGD. Refund = 9.70 - 8.68 = 1.02 SGD, rounded up to the payable 1.05 SGD. That is above the 0.50 SGD de-minimis floor and is 10.5% of the charge, far below the 90% share that would make it a full refund. The outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 1.05, against the SGD 2.00 contested; the remaining charge stands.

NOTHING EXCUSES THE EXCESS. No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-02820-01 is MISSING at weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT (named here as POL-GEN-02(3) requires), so POL-RD-03 cannot be run, and the driver's 'one-way streets' statement cites no artifact and so carries no weight under POL-RD-08. EV-CHAT-02820 holds zero messages, so no rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04; pickup and dropoff amendments are null, so no POL-RD-05; the fare is metered with no quote, so no POL-RD-11; the vehicle is RYDE_X, so no POL-RD-12. EV-FARE-02820 carries no ERP, toll or surcharge line, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing and the 1.02 SGD is distance and time only.

TRACE AND ESCALATION. EV-GPS-02820 is complete — 46 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, maximum gap 0.0 s, no jumps — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. No other POL-RD-10 trigger fires: identifiers and timestamps agree across the artifacts, the refund is far below the 150.00 SGD ceiling and below charged_total, and no charge line is unmatched. Both advocates' kept claims on the excess and on the 1.05 SGD figure are accepted; the rider's claim that the driver's uncited traffic excuse is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation was discarded by the referee for not disclosing the impaired artifact it cited, and nothing turns on it because the same conclusion follows from the driver's failure to cite any artifact at all. Confidence 0.95, above the 0.70 floor. The monetary effect (SGD 1.05) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold and executes automatically.
